item.title: Obvaldo Driving License: Conversion and Exams
item.description: Complete guide to the conversion of the foreign licence in the Canton of Obvaldo: procedure, theoretical and practical examination, compulsory courses and necessary documents.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Conversion of the foreign driver's license is mandatory within 12 months of residency in Switzerland - The Obvaldo Traffic Office manages the procedure with theoretical and practical exams in German - Awareness courses and medical certificate of suitability are required
## Key facts - **What**: Conversion of foreign driving licence to Swiss driving licence in the Canton of Obvaldo - Where: Traffic Office of the Canton of Obvaldo (OW) - Who: Foreign license holders residing in Switzerland - When: Within 12 months of residency (binding term) - Duration of the procedure: 2-3 months on average (passing exams on the first attempt) - Exams: Theoretical (signage/regulation), practical (about 45 minutes), sensitization course (2 days)
In the Canton of Obvaldo, as in the other 25 Swiss cantons, the conversion of the foreign driver's license is regulated by the Federal Law on Road Traffic and managed locally by the competent Traffic Office. Those who hold a license issued abroad and establish themselves as a resident normally have a period of 12 months to convert the document into a valid Swiss license. This term is non-negotiable: once it has expired, the foreign license becomes ineffective on Swiss territory, making driving illegal with significant penalties.
The conversion is not a simple name change of the document. It involves passing a theoretical exam on Swiss road signs and regulations (conducted ### Theoretical Exam and Sensitization Courses
The theoretical exam covers Swiss road signs, cantonal speed limits, priority rules, and parking regulations. For the Canton of Obwalden, the test is conducted in German. Those who do not speak German sufficiently can request linguistic aids (translators or interpreters), although this remains the competence and evaluation of the local Traffic Office.
Sensitization courses are designed to teach drivers accustomed to foreign regulations how to adapt to Swiss road reality. They typically last two days and cover topics such as driver behavior, awareness of specific risks (curves, slopes, slippery surfaces), braking techniques, and technical differences in vehicles circulating in Switzerland. The Traffic Office of Obwalden coordinates the educational offer and recognizes authorized providers. The course is mandatory and must be completed before or during the conversion process.
### Practical Driving Test
The practical driving test lasts approximately 45 minutes and includes sessions in both urban and extra-urban areas. A commission assesses technical skills (use of pedals, gear shifting, parking), awareness of hazards (adequate speed, safe distances, reading of road signs), and respect for Swiss traffic regulations. Passing this step is essential for the issuance of the Swiss definitive driving license. In case of a negative outcome, it is possible to repeat the test according to the modalities established by the office.
### Timelines and Practical Considerations
The complete procedure generally requires 2-3 months, starting from the first presentation to the Traffic Office of Obwalden, assuming the passing of the exams on the first attempt. Delays can accumulate if repeat exams are necessary, if medical documentation is incomplete, or if the sensitization course is not available on requested dates. It is recommended to start the procedure as soon as possible after relocation to avoid approaching the 12-month limit. Once the Swiss driving license is obtained, you can proceed to evaluate the other [administrative expenses associated with relocation](nav:cost-of-living) in the canton.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Conversion Procedure Step by Step
To initiate the conversion of your foreign driving license in the Canton of Obwalden, follow this operational schema:
1. Contact the Traffic Office of Obwalden — Request the official application form for foreign license conversion. Most cantonal offices provide online information or offer assistance upon direct request. Check the office hours and, if possible, schedule an appointment to avoid queues.
**2. Gather Required Documents** — Collect your original driving license, a medical certificate of fitness to drive (issued by a recognized doctor in the canton), a photocopy of your passport or valid ID, and a proof of residence (extract from the civil register, rental agreement, or letter from the local administration).
3. Enroll in a Sensitization Course — The Traffic Office will provide you with a list of authorized course providers. Some offer fixed-date courses (weekly or monthly), while others offer personalized booking. Enroll as soon as possible to avoid missing the 12-month deadline. The course is mandatory and must be completed before the issuance of the new license.
4. Take the Theoretical Exam — Present yourself at the indicated location with the required documents. The exam is computer-based and includes questions on Swiss signage, correct behavior, and local regulations. If necessary, request language assistance when booking the exam.
5. Take the Practical Driving Test — Once you have passed the theoretical exam, you can schedule the practical driving test. The examiner will assess your driving skills according to Swiss standards, including safety, maneuvering, and rule compliance.
6. Collect Your Swiss Driving License — Having passed both exams, the Traffic Office of Obwalden will issue your definitive Swiss driving license, valid for 15 years (standard duration in Switzerland for adult drivers).
### Important Details to Know
A foreign driving license remains valid only for the first 12 months of residence in Switzerland. After this period, driving with an unconverted license is illegal and may result in significant penalties (fine, license revocation, criminal procedure). Some cantons (including Obwalden) require a formal renunciation of the foreign license once the Swiss license is issued, to avoid duplication and clarify which document is valid.
If your foreign license contains medical restrictions (glasses, hearing aids, etc.), these will remain in effect on your new Swiss license. If the restrictions change or you wish to remove them, you must obtain an updated medical certificate and present it to the Traffic Office.

## In a nutshell - The Paul Scherrer Institute in Aargau inaugurated the first sustainable synthetic kerosene plant - Produces 50 litres per day of "zero climate impact" fuel - Airlines today mix 2%, from 2030 mandatory 6%
## Key facts - **What**: Demonstration plant that transforms water, electricity and CO2 into synthetic kerosene - When: Inauguration in 2024 (three-year project) - Where: Paul Scherrer Institut, Aargau (Switzerland) - Who: PSI, Marco Ranocchiari (Head of Laboratory), Federal Office of Civil Aviation, Swiss - Production: 50 litres per day; commercial plant from 2030 in the Netherlands
### The Swiss plant that produces green fuel
The first demonstration plant for the production of synthetic kerosene was inaugurated at the Paul Scherrer Institut (PSI) in Aargau. The plant, the result of three years of research, combines water, electricity and carbon dioxide extracted from sustainable sources to create a fuel "of high quality and with zero climate impact", according to the researchers.
Marco Ranocchiari, head of the technological energies and innovation laboratory AT PSI, describes the result as "a research success, because we have transformed something that was prepared in the laboratory into something bigger". Although the plant produces only 50 liters per day, Ranocchiari points out that it is "practically a miniature commercial plant" where it is possible to conduct tests ### Still prohibitive costs for Swiss passengers
The most urgent challenge for the sector is no longer technological but economic. Jens Fehlinger, CEO of Swiss, points out a concrete and immediate problem: "Prices for sustainable kerosene are four or five times higher than conventional kerosene." This difference in cost has a direct impact on air ticket prices for Swiss passengers and represents the real bottleneck of the energy transition in air transport.
Swiss has confirmed that its planes are already ready for green fuel and could theoretically charge “as much green kerosene as possible from tomorrow”. The problem is that the global supply is insufficient. For this reason, Fehlinger emphasizes the immediate need to accelerate production: "It is essential that we now increase production, to also lower the prices that our passengers ultimately pay."
### Binding timeline until 2050
The stated goal for the aviation sector is to achieve climate neutrality by 2050. This target represents a profound transformation of air mobility, but the intermediate deadlines are already operational and binding:
- **2024 (today)**: Obligation to mix at least 2% sustainable kerosene - 2030: Share rises to 6% (next critical milestone) - 2050: Full climate neutrality target

For passengers flying with Swiss and other Swiss airlines, the change will be gradual but concrete. In the short term (2024-2029), the cost of sustainable fuel will continue to put pressure on ticket prices, even if the mandatory percentage remains contained (2%). The real turning point will come in 2030, when the 6% quota comes into effect and the commercial installation in the Netherlands should be operational.
At that point, the increase in the offer of available sustainable kerosene on the European market may start to reduce costs. If production accelerates as expected, price differentials should decrease gradually towards the end of the decade, even if they will hardly reach parity with fossil kerosene before 2035-2040. Passengers should monitor flight prices towards the end of 2029: if the offer of sustainable fuel is indeed increasing, the effects will start to be felt on tariffs.
### Parallel Innovation: Electric Aircraft
In parallel with the research on synthetic fuel, alternative complementary solutions are emerging. The Swiss Aero-Club celebrated its 125th anniversary by showcasing a Velis Electro, a completely electric aircraft with an autonomy of 50-60 minutes, at Bern.
Although this technology is still in its initial phase and cannot replace commercial long-haul aviation, it represents the attempt to diversify solutions towards climate sustainability.
Matthias Jauslin, president of the Aero-Club, confirms that climate sensitivity has not yet reduced the number of aviation enthusiasts, but the sector is aware of the need to evolve: "With alternative fuels and better aircraft, we are trying to contribute to making aviation more climate-neutral".
### How to Monitor Future Developments
Those working in the Swiss aviation sector and those who fly regularly should keep an eye on regulatory deadlines. The next critical milestone is 2030: if the commercial installation is not operational as expected or if costs do not decrease significantly, the sector may face regulatory blocks or unexpected tariff increases. ## In a nutshell - Legal forms: sole proprietorship, simple company, SA, Sàrl, cooperative - Compulsory registration in the Federal Trade Register within 14 days - Registration costs: CHF 50–300 according to legal form - AVS/AI, LPP, SUVA obligations for employees
## Key facts - **What**: Registration in the Swiss trade register for new businesses - When: Within 14 days from the start of the activity - Where: Office of the Chamber of Commerce in the Obvaldo canton - Who: Independent entrepreneurs and employers with employees - Amount: CHF 50–300 per registration; minimum capital CHF 20,000-100,000 according to form
Starting a business in the Obvaldo Canton requires compliance with well-defined federal and cantonal administrative procedures. The choice of legal form is the first step: sole proprietorship, simple company, public limited company (SA), limited liability company (Sàrl) or cooperative offer different advantages and risks compared to personal liability, taxation and administrative charges.
Once the legal structure has been decided, the next obligation is to register with the Swiss Federal Trade Register. This register, managed at cantonal and municipal level, certifies the legal existence of the company and makes the fundamental data public: name, address, legal form, legal representatives, authorized signature. Registration takes place at the office of the cantonal chamber of commerce (or administrative equivalent) ## Tax and contribution obligations
After registration in the commercial register, the employer assumes obligations towards at least three administrative levels: federal (direct federal tax and VAT), cantonal and municipal (income tax, property tax, possibly exercise tax). The Federal Administration of Customs and Economic Security (FCA) handles direct federal tax and VAT; cantonal administrations handle cantonal and municipal taxes. Each canton, including Obvaldo, defines its own rates and multipliers. Municipalities apply a multiplier calculated on the cantonal rate, determining the total municipal tax.
Value Added Tax (VAT) is managed by the AFC. If the annual turnover exceeds CHF 85,000, VAT registration becomes mandatory. Registration takes place with the Federal Administration through a form available online: the term cannot be deferred and the delay entails a penalty.
### Employee Social Contributions
📊 If the employer hires employees, contributions must be paid by the company:
- **AVS/AI/IPG** (old age, disability, lost maternity earnings): 10.6% of gross salary (the employee pays 5.3%) - Unemployment (AD) and Loss of Earning Allowance (AC): 1.1% up to a federally established annual ceiling - Accident insurance (LAINF/LAA): 0.7-1.5% according to the economic sector - Occupational insurance
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Registration procedure: operational steps Opening a business in the Canton Obwalden follows a precise sequence defined by the Federal Commercial Registry Act (CO, Code of Obligations). Here are the essential steps.
### 1. Documentary preparation Before visiting the Chamber of Commerce office, prepare the following documents: a copy of your identity document (passport, ID card), a draft of the founding act if you intend to establish a company (SA, Sàrl, cooperative), complete details of all partners or shareholders, the definitive address of the company site, a statement of non-opposition from the owner/tenant if the address is rented. For individual businesses, the documentation is reduced: just identity and signature are needed.
### 2. Registration in the commercial register Visit the Chamber of Commerce office in the Canton Obwalden (you can contact the cantonal administration for the exact address). Fill out the official registration form available in paper or online format. Provide an authenticated signature (scanned and authenticated by a notary) and original identity documents or certified copies. The cost varies from CHF 50 to CHF 300 depending on the legal form and complexity. The Canton Obwalden communicates the official tariffs through the competent office.
The ideal deadline is within 14 days of the start of the activity to avoid fines and problems with tax authorities. Once approved, the registration becomes visible in the online public register (managed by the Confederation) within a few days.
### 3. VAT registration If the annual turnover exceeds CHF 85,000, VAT registration is mandatory at the Federal Customs Administration (AFC/ESTV). The form is available online on the federal portal. No delay is allowed: it must be completed once the threshold is reached.
### 4. Registration with cantonal tax offices Contact the cantonal tax administration (director of direct taxes/income tax office) for registration with the cantonal income tax and communal tax. The administration will provide the reference number and payment methods for advance payments, usually in three annual installments.
### 5. Social insurance If you hire employees, the procedure is binding: - **AVS/AI registration**: Contact the AVS central office for registration within 5 days of hiring the first employee. You will receive an affiliation number that must be communicated to the employees. - LPP registration: Contact a recognized pension fund by the canton for registration with the professional pension scheme. Options vary: you can join an employer association or a category fund. - SUVA/LAINF registration: Complete the online form at SUVA or a recognized private insurer.
For each employee, pay the monthly contributions to the AVS office by the 15th of the following month. Failure to pay generates interest and registration in the debtors' register.
### 6. Health insurance Each employee must personally sign up for LAMal within 3 months of the start of employment. The employer does NOT pay the premiums directly: it is the employee's responsibility. However, some employers cover part of the premium as a contractual benefit. The employee must present proof of registration (coverage certificate) by the deadline.
### Key deadlines ⚠️ Here is a summary of the critical deadlines: - Commercial register registration: Within 14 days of the start of the activity - AVS registration (employees): Within 5 days of hiring the first salaried employee - LAMal registration (employees): Within 3 months of the start of employment - VAT registration: Without delay once the CHF 85,000 annual threshold is reached - Registration with cantonal tax office: Ideally within 30 days of the start of the activity - Annual tax declaration: By the deadline set by the Canton Obwalden (usually March 31 of the following year) - Monthly payment of AVS/AI/IPG contributions: By the 15th of the following month
## Support tools To estimate the costs of an employee and tax deductions, use the [salary and tax calculator](nav:calculator). Always consult the Canton Obwalden administration, the Chamber of Commerce office, and local professionals (accountants, notaries) for specific regulatory details and to avoid procedural errors that may result in fines. Many cantons also offer free consultation to new businesses: contact the office directly to find out if it is available.

item.title: AVS in Obvaldo: annuity and complementary services
item.description: How the first pillar and complementary services work in the Obvaldo Canton. An AVS annuity guide.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The cantonal compensation fund manages contributions and contribution gaps in the first pillar. - AVS income calculated on 44 years of contributions (men) and 43 years (women). - Supplementary benefits supplement the annuity up to the minimum living wage in the cantons.
## Key facts - **What**: First federal pillar (AVS) + complementary cantonal benefits - Who: UFAS/BSV (federal) + canton - Where: Switzerland, each canton manages supplementary services independently - Amount: AVS/AI/IPG contributions 5.3% employee (10.6% total with employer) - Period: System in force on 44 years men / 43 years women
### The first pillar in the canton
Swiss social security is divided into three pillars: the first, federal and compulsory, is managed by the Federal Office of Social Insurance (UFAS/BSV) in collaboration with the cantonal compensation funds. In the canton of Obvaldo, as in every Swiss canton, the cantonal compensation fund is responsible for collecting AVS/AI/IPG contributions, recognizing insurance periods and calculating the annuity.
The AVS system guarantees a basic pension to all policyholders who have paid regular contributions during their working life. The annuity is calculated on 44 years of contributions for men and 43 years for women. Any contribution gaps (years without payment or reduced payment) reduce the amount of the final annuity.
### Contribution gaps and coverage
Gaps ### Calculation of the AVS pension and determining factors
The calculation of the AVS pension depends on four factors: the number of years insured, the average insured income, the retirement age, and the sex. The federal minimum pension is fixed, while the maximum is indexed according to the evolution of wages and prices. The UFA/BSV publishes new minimum and maximum amounts every year to maintain the purchasing power.
Regularly paid contributions are tracked by the cantonal compensation fund on an individual insurance account. Employers pay 5.3% of the salary as a dependent contribution, while employers pay an additional 5.3%, for a total of 10.6%. Freelancers pay 9.8% of their taxable income. A year is considered a year with a gap if the contributions paid are less than 10% of the annual maximum. It is essential to check your AVS insurance account at least every five years to identify errors or gaps, reporting discrepancies immediately to the compensation fund.
### Minimum vital and complementary benefits
In the canton of Obwalden, as in all Swiss cantons, it is the responsibility of the cantonal administration to verify if an AVS pension is sufficient to cover the minimum vital. If not, complementary benefits (PC) integrate the pension until reaching the minimum threshold. The minimum vital varies from canton to canton, based on local living costs and cantonal social policies.
A contributory gap corresponds to a full year in which no contributions were paid or were paid in reduced measure. Every gap entails a percentage reduction of the final pension. For example, 5 gaps out of 44 years represent an average reduction of the maximum pension. It is possible to fill gaps within certain time limits by voluntarily paying contributions to the cantonal compensation fund. You can use the [AVS calculator](nav:pension) to obtain an estimate of your pension based on the real data of your insurance account.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to Request Complementary Benefits
To request complementary benefits in the canton of Obvaldo, the first step is to submit a request to the competent cantonal office, usually the social security or social assistance office of the canton. The request must include: a copy of the AVS pension decision, the last three months' bank statement, documentation of medical and housing expenses, and a declaration of the assets and income of all members of the household.
The cantonal office has a legal deadline to examine the request, usually 30-45 days. During this period, it may request additional documentation. Once approved, the complementary benefits will take effect from the first day of the month in which the request was submitted, in some cases from an earlier date if there are specific reasons.
### Check Your Account and Contacts
Before thinking about complementary benefits, it is advisable to check your AVS insurance account with the cantonal compensation fund of your canton. You can consult it online through the cantonal AVS portal or in person at the compensation office. If you find contributory gaps, report them immediately to the fund to check if they are due to administrative errors or if they can be filled with voluntary contributions.
The cantonal compensation fund provides free consultation on the calculation of projected pension (useful for planning retirement), the possibility of filling contributory gaps, and the modalities of requesting complementary benefits. Use the [AVS pension calculator](nav:pension) to get an accurate estimate based on the real data of your account.

item.title: Calculation of AVS annuity and contribution gaps
item.description: How the cantonal compensation fund works in the calculation of the AVS annuity, what contribution gaps reduce the amount and how the supplementary benefits fill the living minimum.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The cantonal compensation fund manages the calculation of the AVS annuity in the first Swiss pillar - Contribution gaps reduce the amount of the annuity in proportion to the missing months - Supplementary benefits guarantee coverage of the minimum living allowance when the income is insufficient - The application process starts 3-4 months before reaching retirement age
## Key facts - What: Cantonal compensation fund in charge of calculating and paying the AVS annuity - When: Request for annuity 3-4 months before the reference age (64 years old men, 63 years old women) - Where: At the compensation fund of the canton of residence (Obvaldo or other) - Who: UFAS/BSV coordinates at federal level; cantonal coffers manage locally - Amount: Depends on contributions paid during the working career and contribution gaps - Duration: Minimum 1 year contribution to access the annuity; full career typically 44 years for men - Procedure: Documentation sent automatically; return of form required at least 2 months before the desired date
In the Swiss social security system, the first pillar (AVS) represents the basis of security in old age. Each canton has its own cantonal compensation fund in charge of managing the calculation of the AVS annuity for its residents. The fund collects and records contributions during the entire working career and, upon reaching the age of The calculation of the AVS pension follows well-defined steps at the federal level, even if materially carried out at the cantonal level. The amount of the annuity depends on two main factors: the number of years of contribution credited to the insurance account and the average coordinated income over the entire working career.
The system is progressive: it is not enough to have paid many contributions at all, but the continuity and duration of the contributory career counts. A worker who enters the labour market late will access a lower income than a colleague who started earlier, even if both have paid the same total amount of contributions during their employment. This federal mechanism encourages career continuity and favors those who access work at a young age. Similarly, the [secondo pilastro (LPP/BVG)](nav:pension) completes the social security coverage with mandatory payments from the employer.
### The concrete impact of contribution gaps
A common scenario concerns job search periods between jobs. Even a few consecutive months of unemployment, if not covered by unemployment insurance, create a gap in the AVS tax register. Although a single 6-month gap has a seemingly modest impact, the accumulation of multiple gaps over the course of the career can reduce final performance by a significant percentage.
For example, if an insured person turns 44 years of contribution (instead of 45 years of a
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). How to request the AVS pension and check contributory gaps
The procedure for requesting the AVS pension begins about 3-4 months before reaching the reference age. The cantonal compensation fund sends automatically to the insured a complete package containing the request form, a detailed extract of the contributions account (where all identified gaps in the system are highlighted) and operational instructions.
**Step-by-step procedure for requesting the pension:
1. Accurate verification of the extract: Check the document received from the cantonal fund in every detail to identify any gaps, unregistered contributions or discrepancies in the coordinated income. If you notice inconsistent data or missing contributions, contact the cantonal fund immediately to request a correction. This phase is critical because errors can permanently reduce the pension.
2. Evaluate the opportunity to fill gaps: Request the cantonal fund to project the monthly increase in pension that would result from paying voluntary contributions. Compare the total cost to be paid with the annual increase in pension and the number of years of life expectancy to retirement to evaluate whether it is worth it.
3. Complete and sign the request form: Return the signed form to the cantonal fund within the specified times (usually at least 2 months before the desired retirement date). Attach any payment for voluntary contributions if you decide to fill gaps.
4. Receive the communication and start of the pension: The cantonal fund will formally communicate the definitive amount of the pension, the exact date of commencement (first day of the month following the reference age) and the payment methods (usually through a bank account).
### Complementary benefits: the backstop of the minimum vital
When the AVS pension, possibly integrated with other incomes (LPP, third pillar, real estate income, widow's pensions), does not reach the minimum vital established at the cantonal level, the cantonal complementary benefits intervene automatically to fill the gap. This is a financial assistance funded by general taxation (federal and cantonal), not a pension contribution.
Complementary benefits mainly cover: rent and housing expenses (up to a cantonal maximum), contributions to the compulsory health insurance (LAMal) through provincial subsidies to the premium, and home care expenses for those who require continuous medical support. Access is subject to income and asset verification according to uniform federal criteria. It is not an automatic benefit: it must be explicitly requested at the competent cantonal office, even simultaneously with the request for the AVS pension.
Next practical steps:
Contact the cantonal compensation fund of Obvaldo at least 3-4 months before the desired retirement date to receive the official extract of the contributions account and the request documentation. If you anticipate having paid contributions in other Swiss cantons or if you have worked abroad and paid contributions to foreign systems, report it immediately: the cantonal fund will coordinate with other entities to ensure the complete computation of the contributory career according to international treaties.

The Swiss economy showed a clear sign of strength during the month of July 2026. According to official data released by the Federal Office of Customs and Border Security (FOCS), Swiss exports recorded a marked recovery, interrupting a phase of stagnation that had lasted for several months. The total value of goods sold abroad reached CHF 27.8 billion, an increase of 13.8% compared to the previous month, net of seasonal effects. Considering the correction for price trends, real growth stands at 10.7%.
## # Trade Volume Analysis This result marks the highest level achieved by exports since March 2025. At the same time, the import front has presented an opposite sign: the value of goods in The analysis of data released by the FOCBS highlights a strong disparity between the various commodity sectors of the national economy. The main driver of this expansion was the chemical-pharmaceutical sector. In this specific area, exports recorded an increase of 3.3 billion francs in a single month, equivalent to a 25% growth. This contribution was decisive in balancing the weakness of other industrial sectors. The watchmaking sector also provided a positive boost, showing a clear increase in cross-border sales. Conversely, the situation remains different for other key segments of the Swiss market: foreign deliveries of machinery, electronic products, and equipment have remained in a phase of substantial stagnation.

item.title: Residence Permit B: Requirements and Renewal
item.description: Permit B allows renewable residence in Switzerland. Complete guide on requirements, documents, duration and renewal procedure at federal and cantonal level.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Permit B is a renewable temporary residence category for foreigners in Switzerland - Duration varies according to citizenship: from 1 to 5 years typically - Renewal must be requested at the cantonal migration office before the deadline
## Key facts - **What**: Residence permit category B - Feature: Renewable residence - Competent authority: Federal SEM + cantonal offices - Duration: 1 to 5 years depending on origin - Who issues it: Canton (with federal coordination)
### What is residence permit B
Residence permit B allows foreigners to reside and work in Switzerland on a temporary but renewable basis. At the federal level, the legislation on foreign permits (SEM) recognizes three main categories: the L permit (short duration, up to 1 year), the B permit (renewable residence) and the C permit (permanent residence). Permit B falls between these two extremes: it is not a permanent authorisation, but at the same time it allows longer periods of stay and continuous work, with the possibility of renewal at the end of each period.
The management of the B permit involves both the federal administration (through the SEM) and the cantonal authorities. The Obvaldo canton, like all Swiss cantons, has a migration office in charge of investigating applications, verifying the requirements and issuing the permit according to federal directives and cantonal legislation. The procedural specifications for the ### Differences between permit B and permit C
To understand the permit B, it is useful to compare it with the permit C. The permit of domicile C is intended for foreigners who intend to settle permanently in Switzerland. Normally, the transition to permit C occurs after 10 years of continuous residence with permit B, or after 5 years for EU/EEA citizens. The permit C does not have an expiration date (remains valid until revocation) and does not require periodic renewal. The permit B, on the other hand, is time-limited and requires renewal every 1-5 years.
This distinction has important practical implications. Those who have permit B must plan the renewal in advance and continuously verify the maintenance of the requirements (stable employment, payment of social contributions, health insurance). Those who have permit C benefit from greater legal stability, even if they continue to be bound by Swiss federal and cantonal laws.
### Procedures and documentation
The procedure for permit B usually involves the submission of a written application to the competent cantonal migration office. The required documentation varies depending on the individual situation and cantonal regulations, but generally includes: an official application form, a copy of the passport or valid identity document, a contract of employment or a letter from the employer confirming the employment, a proof of accommodation (rental contract or statement from the owner), and a certificate of social contributions (AVS/AI) if available.
Some cantons also require a statement on any previous convictions and a medical certificate of good health. The deadlines for submitting the documentation and response times vary: it is essential to check the specific requirements at the Obwalden cantonal office or through the federal SEM portal.
### Obligations during permit B
During the validity period of permit B, the foreigner is required to maintain certain obligations. They must maintain employment or otherwise a stable source of income (whose amount is not fixed by federal regulations, but may vary by canton). item.title: Inheritance and donation tax: the Svitto rates
item.description: How inheritance and gift tax works in the Canton of Schwyz: rates for degree of kinship, exemptions and deadlines for declaration.
item.content:encoded:
## At a glance - Inheritance and gift taxes are CANTONAL in Switzerland, not federal - In the Canton of Schwyz, tax rates vary according to the beneficiary's degree of kinship - Spouses and direct descendants benefit from exemptions or reduced rates - The inheritance declaration must comply with specific deadlines set by cantonal law
## Key facts - **What**: Cantonal inheritance and gift taxes, graduated by kinship class - Where: Canton of Schwyz, in Central Switzerland - Who: Heirs, donors, Schwyz cantonal tax administration - When: Upon transfer of assets via inheritance or gift, with declaration within cantonal deadlines - Legal basis: Schwyz cantonal laws and ordinances (not federal) - Exemptions: Surviving spouse and direct descendants benefit from a privileged regime
In Switzerland, inheritance and gift taxes are not regulated at the federal level but remain the EXCLUSIVE competence of the cantons. In the Canton of Schwyz, as in the other twenty-six Swiss cantons, the tax structure for successions follows its own rules defined by specific cantonal laws.
The rate system in the Canton of Schwyz varies significantly based on the degree of kinship between the deceased (or donor) and the beneficiary. Spouses and direct descendants — children, grandchildren — receive preferential tax treatment, often with total exemptions or significantly reduced rates, while more distant relatives and unrelated persons are subject to higher progressive rates.
### How the Swiss cantonal system works
Cantonal inheritance and gift taxes in Switzerland operate on the principle of CANTONAL AUTONOMY. Each canton independently defines: - Who is subject to the tax (residence, location of assets) - Kinship classes and associated rates - Exemptions (often broad for spouses and descendants) - Minimum tax-free amounts (allowances) - Deadlines for declaration and payment
This cantonal differentiation reflects the Swiss federal structure, where civil law — including inheritance matters — is coordinated at the federal level through the Swiss Civil Code, but tax law is regulated locally.
In the Canton of Schwyz, as in almost all cantons, it is common for the surviving spouse to be completely exempt from inheritance tax, while children and direct descendants benefit from reduced rates or exemptions up to certain amounts. More distant relatives (siblings, aunts/uncles, cousins) and unrelated individuals are subject to significantly higher rates. For an integrated view of your financial situation, you can also explore the role of [supplementary AHV/BVG pension planning in succession planning](nav:pension).
The choice of these regimes is left entirely to cantonal political decisions, and Swiss cantons show great variety: some have very progressive systems with broad exemptions, while others maintain higher taxes across all classes. In the Canton of Schwyz, decisions regarding rates and allowances are made by the cantonal administration according to the current cantonal tax law. It is important to note that the Swiss system differs radically from that of other European countries, where inheritance tax may be federal or national: in Switzerland, this matter remains exclusively under the control of the cantons. ## Practical implications for those inheriting in the Canton of Schwyz
For a person inheriting assets from a relative in the Canton of Schwyz, the importance of the local tax scheme is immediate. The final amount of the available inheritance depends significantly on the degree of kinship with the deceased and the tax rates applied according to current cantonal regulations.
### Kinship classes and graduated rates
The Swiss inheritance tax system universally uses the criterion of 'degree of kinship' as the central element to calculate the applicable rate. In the Canton of Schwyz, as in other cantons, kinship classes are organized according to standard schemes:
Class I — Spouse and direct descendants: includes the surviving spouse, children, and grandchildren. It benefits from the lowest rates or total exemptions, reflecting the intent to protect the family unit.
Class II — Ascendants and collaterals: includes parents, brothers, sisters, and their descendants. Subject to intermediate rates, significantly higher than Class I.
Class III — Other relatives and non-relatives: includes distant relatives and unrelated persons. Subject to progressively higher rates.
Each class has an associated specific rate: Class I benefits from substantial reductions or total exemptions, Class II from intermediate rates, and Class III from much higher rates. Furthermore, each class generally has a tax-free allowance (an untaxed amount), below which no tax is paid.
### Exemptions for spouse and descendants
In the Canton of Schwyz, as in most Swiss cantons, the surviving spouse almost always benefits from a complete or near-total exemption from inheritance tax. This legislative choice reflects the intent to protect the family unit and ensure the surviving spouse the peaceful enjoyment of the common assets.
Children and other direct descendants often benefit from generous allowances — amounts below which no tax is paid — and significantly reduced rates compared to distant relatives. These allowances and rates, however, vary from canton to canton and may be subject to legislative changes.
Regarding donations (transfers of assets made during the donor's lifetime), many cantons apply regimes similar to successions, although often with slightly different rates and shorter review periods. A donation made during the donor's lifetime may be recalculated and taxed together with the succession if other donations occur within certain periods.
### Considerations for multi-cantonal tax planning
Given the differentiation between cantons, those who own assets in multiple cantons or are planning an inheritance must consider the regulations of EACH involved canton. If a person residing in the Canton of Schwyz owns real estate in another canton, they are subject to taxation both in Schwyz (for movable assets and resident wealth) and in the other canton (for the real estate located there). This complexity makes conscious and documented succession planning essential. To verify the overall impact on your taxes, you can consult the [complete guide to tax returns](nav:tax-return) to understand how inheritances integrate into your cantonal tax framework.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Operational procedure: how to declare an inheritance in the Canton of Schwyz
In the Canton of Schwyz, as in all Swiss cantons, the succession procedure follows well-defined and administratively binding steps.
### Step 1 — Declaring the inheritance to the competent cantonal offices
When a succession opens (upon the death of the owner), the heirs have a legal obligation to declare the inherited assets to the cantonal tax administration of Schwyz within a specific deadline. The exact terms vary according to the applicable cantonal law and are communicated by the municipality of residence of the deceased. The declaration must include a complete and detailed list of assets (real estate, bank accounts, securities, insurance policies, other valuables), accompanied by ownership certificates and estimated valuations, as well as documentation of the degree of kinship between the deceased and the beneficiaries.
### Step 2 — Tax calculation according to cantonal rates
Once the declaration is received, the cantonal tax administration proceeds to calculate the applicable tax, systematically considering: the beneficiary's kinship class, the total value of the inheritance, the exemptions and allowances provided by cantonal law, the progressively applied rates according to the statutory brackets, as well as any tax credits or deductions.
### Step 3 — Notification, appeal, and payment
The cantonal administration notifies the amount due to the heirs through a formal administrative decision. The heirs proceed with the payment according to the methods and terms indicated (generally via payment slip). In case of disagreement regarding the calculated amount, the kinship classification, or other aspects of taxation, it is possible to file an appeal (within the legal deadlines) to the competent cantonal authorities, usually the cantonal tax appeal office.
### Necessary documents and certificates
For a correct declaration in the Canton of Schwyz, it is advisable to prepare and gather the following documents in a timely manner: - Original will (if available) or legal succession documentation - Original death certificate and civil status certificates of all heirs - Ownership and title documents (real estate deeds, bank certificates, insurance policies, investment securities) - Written valuations of movable assets (jewelry, art, collections) if quantitatively significant - Official documentation of the degree of kinship (birth certificates, marriage certificates, civil registers) - Statements of current accounts and deposits at the time of death
### Where to go for administrative advice
For specific information on current rates, applied allowances, precise deadlines, and forms in the Canton of Schwyz, it is necessary to contact the cantonal financial administration directly (in German: Abteilung Finanzen of the Canton of Schwyz; in Italian: Divisione Finanze del Canton Svitto) or the municipality of residence of the deceased, as they are the bodies that directly manage cantonal inheritance and gift taxes. Every Swiss municipality has an office in charge of coordinating succession procedures, providing free advice on the necessary documentation, assisting in filling out declaration forms, and guiding heirs through the entire administrative process.
The variety of Swiss cantonal systems makes it essential to carefully verify the regulations applicable in the canton concerned. There is no 'federal inheritance tax' in Switzerland: taxation is EXCLUSIVELY cantonal, therefore the rules of Schwyz do not apply in other cantons and the rules of other cantons do not apply in Schwyz. For complex succession planning, especially in the case of assets located in multiple cantons, significant estates, or complex family situations, it is advisable to consult a specialized tax advisor or a lawyer experienced in Swiss succession law, as the financial implications can be significant and opportunities for legal optimization merit professional assessment.

## In a nutshell - Legal forms: single company, SNC, SA, SARL/GmbH, association - Commercial register: mandatory federal registration managed cantonally - Three tax tiers: Federal IFD, Cantonal Taxes, Municipal Taxes - Social security: AVS/AI mandatory, LPP optional, LAMal mandatory
## Key facts - **What**: Business registration in the Swiss trade register - When: Before starting self-employment - Where: Office of the Registrar of Commerce of the Canton of Switzerland - Who: Entrepreneurs, sole proprietorships, joint-stock companies - Tax levels: Federal (DFI + VAT), cantonal, municipal - AVS/AI contributions: 9.8% of net income for self-employed - Minimum capital: CHF 100,000 for SA (CHF20,000 paid-in), CHF 20,000 for SARL
In the canton of Swabia, as in every Swiss canton, anyone wishing to engage in an independent economic activity must register with the commercial register. This is a federal rule implemented at the cantonal level: the register is centralized at the competent office of the canton, where the data of all companies active in the territory converge.
Registration in the commercial register is not just an administrative formality: it represents the moment when the company acquires civil rights, allows you to open a company bank account and — crucially — activates tax and social security obligations. This is why it is essential to register BEFORE starting the activity, not after.
### Which legal form to choose?
The law ### The three-tier tax system
The most important element in running a Swiss business is understanding the three-tier tax system. The Swiss Confederation applies direct federal tax (DFI) on the net income of the company. Each canton adds a cantonal income and profit tax. Each municipality, in turn, applies a municipal tax with a multiplier applied to the cantonal rate. The result is that the tax burden varies significantly between cantons and municipalities.
In the canton of Svitto, as in all cantons, the cantonal administration sets the cantonal rate; the municipalities then establish their own multiplier. This means that two identical companies could pay very different taxes depending on where they are located. It is therefore essential to check the specific rates at the cantonal tax office and at the municipality where you intend to locate the registered office.
Value added tax (VAT) is managed at the federal level by the Federal Administration of Customs (AFC/ESTV). A business must register for VAT if it exceeds CHF 100,000 in annual turnover. The ordinary rate is 8.1%. Registering for VAT entitles you to the deduction of taxes paid on goods and services purchased (accounting savings), but requires more complex quarterly statements and annual returns.
### Social security and insurance: the essential obligations
Every independent in Switzerland MUST register with the AVS/AI (Social Security
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Procedure step-by-step: from idea to registration
To start a business in the canton of Schwyz, you must follow a precise procedure. Here are the essential steps.
Step 1: Choose the legal form. Consult a notary, accountant or the cantonal commercial office to understand which form is most suitable. The choice depends on available capital, number of partners, and risk profile. If you are unsure, speak with a professional.
Step 2: Register with the commercial register. Complete the registration form and deposit it with the Schwyz Commercial Register Office (decentralized offices, if present, accept registrations). It is mandatory to register BEFORE starting the activity. Registration creates your federal business identity (IDE number, Business Identification Number).
Step 3: Open a business bank account. Once registered with the commercial register, open a business bank account in the company's name. Banks in Switzerland require a copy of the commercial register as proof of the company's existence.
Step 4: Register with the AVS. Go to the competent municipal office (the municipality where you reside if you are self-employed; the municipality of the legal seat if you are a company) and register with the AVS. You will receive a business AVS number and will receive notifications on the contributions due.
Step 5: Sign the health insurance (LAMal). Contact a health insurance fund within 3 months of the first day of activity. You can choose from various deductible and insurance models. Do not wait: the obligation is immediate, and the lack of coverage exposes you to penalties.
Step 6: Register for VAT (if applicable). If the expected turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 per year, register with the Federal Administration of Customs (AFC/ESTV) for VAT. You can do this online through the federal portal.
Step 7: Verify specific sector insurance obligations. If you hire employees, the accident insurance (LAInf) becomes mandatory. Contact SUVA or private insurers authorized in your sector to obtain a policy.
### Checklist of control
- [ ] Commercial register registration form completed and signed - [ ] Business bank account opened with a Swiss bank - [ ] IDE number (Business Identification Number) received - [ ] AVS registration completed at the municipality - [ ] Active health insurance (confirmation from the health insurance fund) - [ ] Determination of federal, cantonal, and municipal IFD rates - [ ] Accounting and taxation plan prepared - [ ] Accident insurance signed (if with employees)
### Administrative times and deadlines
The entire basic registration process (commercial register + AVS + LAMal) can take 2-4 weeks, depending on the speed of local bureaucracy. Start in advance of the planned first day of activity. Each canton and municipality has slightly different times, so contact the Schwyz offices directly to confirm the exact deadlines.

item.title: Complementary services Unscrewed: AVS and vital minimum
item.description: Guide to the calculation of the AVS annuity, contribution gaps and supplementary benefits in the Canton of Schwyz. Role of the cantonal clearing house and practical procedures to ensure minimum viability.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Supplementary benefits (PC) supplement the AVS when the annuity does not cover the minimum living - The cantonal compensation fund manages registration of contributions, gaps and PC coordination - In the canton of Schwyz, the CPs are financed by the Confederation, canton and municipalities - Contribution gaps and low incomes are the main causes of access to PCs
## Key facts - **What**: Supplementary benefits integrated into the AVS annuity to ensure minimum living - When: Requests during or after retirement (reference age: 64 women, 65 men) - Where: Canton of Svitto via cantonal compensation fund - Who: Crooked residents with insufficient AVS income - Amount: Calculated as the difference between living minimum and rent plus lump sums for rentals and LAMal - Management: Federal Social Insurance Office coordinates; cantonal administration examines applications
In the canton of Svitto, the cantonal compensation fund is the central body of the first pillar of social security (AVS). It manages the collection of contributions, the recording of insurance periods, the calculation of annuities and coordinates access to supplementary benefits (PC) for residents.
When the monthly AVS annuity does not cover the actual costs of living, supplementary benefits intervene to ensure the minimum living. This system ensures that no pensioner in the canton falls below the poverty line, as long as they apply and meet the requirements ### How to Calculate AVS Rent and the Role of Contribution Gaps
The monthly AVS income depends on two main factors: the amount of the average salary recorded during the contribution years and the number of years of contributions paid. A full insurance period for men is 45 years; for women 44 years.
When an insured has worked fewer years than necessary, or has had periods without payments, the compensation fund records "contribution gaps". These gaps directly reduce the amount of the final monthly annuity. A common scenario concerns those who have interrupted their career for family reasons, illness or unemployment without contributory coverage.
Not all gaps count equally. The case distinguishes between: - ** Justified gaps **: periods covered by contributions due to sickness, invalidity, unemployment, maternity when accredited by the system - Unjustified gaps: periods of total absence from the system, sometimes recoverable retroactively through voluntary payments
### Voluntary Deposit Strategies
Those who discover that they have gaps before retirement can pay additional voluntary contributions to the compensation fund, thus increasing their monthly income. After retirement, recovery is generally more difficult and subject to tighter administrative terms.
The swift compensation fund offers free advice to calculate the cost and benefit of a payment
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### How to Apply for Complementary Benefits in the Canton of Schwyz
The process for accessing complementary benefits in the Canton of Schwyz usually begins several months before the expected retirement date.
Phase 1: Request a Payout Estimate — Contact the cantonal compensation fund and request an extract of your insurance account (Versichertenkonto). This document shows all contributory periods, gaps, and the estimated payout at the time of retirement. You can also obtain this document online through the cantonal compensation fund's portal.
**Phase 2: Verify Gaps** — Carefully examine the extract. If you notice missing periods (unregistered work years), report this immediately to the fund with supporting documents (pay slips, contracts). You have a deadline to submit appeals or provide clarifications.
Phase 3: Decision on Additional Contributions — If your payout will be below the minimum vital amount, consider with the fund whether it makes sense to pay voluntary contributions in the months leading up to retirement. The fund will calculate how much to pay to achieve a more adequate payout.
Phase 4: Application for Complementary Benefit — About 3-4 months before retirement, submit a written application to the Canton of Schwyz's Complementary Benefits Office. Attach: - AVS (AVS payout certificate) received from the fund after the final review - Declaration of income and assets (cantonally issued form) - Certificate of mandatory health insurance (LAMal) - Recent bank statements if required
Phase 5: Decision and Payment — The cantonal office examines the application within 2-4 weeks. If approved, the PCs are paid automatically along with the AVS payout from the first month of retirement.
### Deadlines, Documents, and Contacts
There is no absolute deadline for submitting a PC application if already retired, but it is recommended to do so no later than the month following retirement. Those who submit late may be entitled to retroactive PCs, but only if the application is processed within the administrative deadlines set by the canton.
The cantonal compensation fund provides specific forms and consultants who can guide you through the process. Many offer free telephone consultations on voluntary payment options and personal payout estimates. It is recommended to contact the fund at least 6-12 months before the expected retirement date to plan accordingly.
